questions.q: What is this capstone, structurally, compared to the courses earlier in the Salesforce Administrator path?
options: A separate set of 20 unrelated exercises, one per Salesforce feature
One continuous, real Salesforce implementation built for a single fictional company across all 20 lessons
A multiple-choice review of the earlier courses with no hands-on building
A single lesson that summarizes the entire path
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit: this capstone is one continuous build for one fictional company, applying skills from every earlier course together, not disconnected exercises.

questions.q: Per the Definition of Done, which chapter is responsible for implementing the role hierarchy, profiles, and sharing rules?
options: Chapter 4 — Analytics and Delivery
Chapter 1 — Design
Chapter 3 — Build: Automation and Security
Chapter 2 — Build: Data and Objects
questions.explain: The requirements table maps the role hierarchy, profiles, and sharing rules requirement to Chapter 3, where the security model designed in Chapter 1 gets implemented.

questions.q: Why does Chapter 1 focus on design before any configuration happens in Setup?
options: Because Setup is locked until a design document is uploaded
Because real implementation projects fail when an admin starts clicking before deciding what the data and security models should look like
Because Salesforce requires a signed design document before objects can be created
Because custom objects cannot be created without a prior Flow
questions.explain: The lesson states directly that a real implementation project fails when an admin opens Setup before deciding what the data model and security model should look like, which is why Chapter 1 does the design work first.

questions.q: According to this lesson, which of these is NOT one of the ten Definition of Done requirements?
options: At least two custom objects modeling something the standard objects don't cover
A certified Salesforce Administrator credential issued at the end of the course
An approval process for a real approval scenario at the company
Reports organized into folders plus an executive dashboard
questions.explain: The ten requirements are all about the org itself (data model, security, automation, reports, sample data, testing, documentation) -- issuing a certification is never one of them, and LTV Academy does not issue Salesforce certifications.

questions.q: What does "portfolio-ready" mean for this specific capstone, beyond the org simply not throwing errors?
options: Having the most custom objects of any student's org
Using a different fictional company example in every chapter to show range
One consistent scenario used throughout, a build the student can explain and defend, and real artifacts like a data model diagram and a written retrospective
Completing the lessons as fast as possible
questions.explain: The lesson defines portfolio-ready as one consistent scenario from Lesson 2 through Lesson 20, a defensible build, and real artifacts -- not just an error-free org.
